messages:
Morgan: heads-up — seeing repeat NCCL/connectivity errors for multi-gpu allreduce in eu-central g5-pool over the last 25m. jobs moving to TCP fallback but perf tanking. logs show ibv_create_cq and IBV_DEVICE_FATAL sometimes. anyone else?
Raghav: saw a few alerts, investigating. which hosts?
Morgan: node list in thread: g5-eu-012, g5-eu-019, g5-eu-020. errors: 
```
NCCL WARN Call to ibv_reg_mr failed: Input/output error
ibv_create_cq: -22
nccl_net.c: NCCL_NET_GDR_OPEN_FAIL
```
Emma: thanks — quick q: did we recently roll kernel or mlx firmware in eu-central?
Morgan: yeah, kernel bumped to 6.2.14 across a subset ~1h before initial failures. not the whole pool.
Li: interesting — partial kernel roll = asymmetric stack. RDMA/PMTU sensitive. can you paste `ibv_devinfo` output from a bad and a good node?
Morgan: grabbing now. bad node (g5-eu-019):
```
$ ibv_devinfo -v
hca_id: mlx5_0
transport: InfiniBand (link layer: Ethernet)
fw_ver: 16.36.1040
phys_port_cnt: 2
link_layer: Ethernet
port 1:
  state: ACTIVE (4)
  max_mtu: 4096 (4)
  active_mtu: 2048 (3)
```
Good node (g5-eu-012):
```
$ ibv_devinfo -v
hca_id: mlx5_0
transport: InfiniBand (link layer: Ethernet)
fw_ver: 16.36.1040
phys_port_cnt: 2
link_layer: Ethernet
port 1:
  state: ACTIVE (4)
  max_mtu: 4096 (4)
  active_mtu: 4096 (4)
```
Raghav: active_mtu mismatch — that smells like a PMTU/VXLAN fragmentation problem. did the kernel change split off vxlan offloads or change GRO/TSO defaults?
Emma: dev to netops — Taylor, any recent TOR/overlay changes?
Taylor: nothing intentional in TOR config. but we saw a VXLAN offload autoprobe on the ToR switch this morning from vendor firmware. checking logs.
infra-bot: kernel-rollout job #eu-cent-6.2 applied to 12 hosts at 2026-03-20T09:42:17Z 
Li: possible sequence: kernel change on host -> NIC/driver negotiated different offload behavior -> VXLAN/overlay path drops large RDMA UDP frames -> IB stack reports MR/register/create_cq failures -> NCCL falls back or errors.
Morgan: repro: if active_mtu < expected, nccl allreduce fails fast. can force fallback with `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` but that's 4-5x slower.
Raghav: agree. short-term mitigation: set net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1? that fixes TCP PMTU but RDMA RoCE uses underlying MTU — need to ensure encapsulation doesn't fragment.
Emma: can we try disabling VXLAN offloads on the vxlan device on the bad nodes? `ethtool -K vxlan0 tx off rx off gso off gro off` — that tends to avoid HW putting bigger frames into fabric.
Morgan: applying to g5-eu-019 now (rolling to one node for test).
Morgan: ran:
```
sudo ethtool -K vxlan0 tx off rx off gso off gro off
sudo sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=134217728
sudo sysctl -w net.core.wmem_max=134217728
```
Morgan: restarted the failing job — prelim success, allreduce progressed without ibv_create_cq errors.
Raghav: good signal. need to confirm at scale. can netops confirm no TOR behavior will re-enable offload?
Taylor: vendor confirmed an autoprobe on a subset of ToRs after firmware patch — it re-enabled segmentation offloads for tunnels. I'll disable autoprobe and push a conservative profile.
Li: long-term we should avoid asymmetric kernel/driver stack in a single pool. options: pin kernel/driver by rack or do canary then full rollout. also add a validation step for `ibv_devinfo` active_mtu parity pre-rollout.
Emma: also add a probe during host join: check `active_mtu` and if < configured expected, mark host as degraded and don't schedule multi-node RDMA jobs.
Morgan: noted. for immediate runbook I'll add a nodetool that runs at boot and a cron to ensure vxlan offload state matches expected.
Raghav: one more datapoint — logs also show occasional `mlx5_core: failed to set rx cqe` warnings on the bad nodes, probably driver/firmware mismatch. firmware looks same, so kernel driver change likely.
Taylor: vendor: if we revert kernel on those nodes, will offload behavior match old state? or do they recommend specific module params? I'll coordinate rollback window.
Li: rollback is invasive during peak. intermediate plan: 1) set vxlan offloads off on all rolled nodes; 2) tag rolled nodes as RDMA-degraded in scheduler; 3) keep working with Taylor on ToR autoprobe settings and vendor follow-up.
Emma: created ticket INFRA-5279 with steps and a small health-check script. assigning Morgan/Taylor/Raghav.
Morgan: thanks — I'll run the offload toggle across the ten affected nodes one-by-one and update ticket with timestamps.
Taylor: pushed ToR rollback plan, will schedule vendor change window tonight.
infra-bot: scheduled maintenance window INFRA-MNT-2026-03-20-23:00-00:30 for vendor ToR firmware rollback (affected: eu-central)
Raghav: follow-up: please capture `ethtool -S` and `dmesg | grep mlx5` before/after on a pair of nodes so we can file a proper vendor bug.
Morgan: will collect and attach to INFRA-5279. for now, setting `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` as a temporary fallback for customers hitting failures and marking nodes as degraded.
Li: thanks team. lesson: partial rollouts + tunneling offloads = subtle RDMA breakage. add to rollout checklist. :white_check_mark:
